title: Compatible local comparison maps from dual exterior conormal to self Ext
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], V an open of Z and n a natural number. Assume every point of V has an affine neighborhood in Y whose immersion ideal [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put C=i*ker(i) [def-pc-module-pullback], B=i_*O_Z, G=H^n(RHom_Y(B[0],B[0])) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], T=(i*G)|V and F=dual(exteriorSheaf(C,n))|V [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. There are neighborhoods W_z of every point z of V and module-sheaf morphisms φ_z:F.over W_z→T.over W_z on the localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Each point z lies in W_z. On every open U contained in both W_x and W_y, the components of φ_x and φ_y agree. On every open U contained in W_x the component of φ_x is surjective on sections. No global sheaf morphism is asserted.

proof.text: On a regular affine chart resolve A/I by the actual augmented Koszul projective resolution. Sheafify its augmentation and use open restriction of derived internal Hom and the bounded-above finite-free Hom model. The differential of Hom(K,A/I) is zero, since every generator lies in I. Thus degree-n cohomology is Hom_A(wedge^n A^m,A/I), which equals Hom_(A/I)(wedge^n((A/I)^m),A/I).

Identify (A/I)^m with I/I² by the regular conormal basis. This identifies the preceding module with the dual of wedge^n(I/I²). Sheafifying identifies it with dual(exteriorSheaf C n) on the inverse-image chart, where C=i*ker(i). The quotient scalar action is the usual A/I action, so the tensor pullback after cohomology gives that same module.

On overlaps first refine around each point so that the two regular conormal bases have equal length and their coordinate change is invertible. Construct every degree of the Koszul chain map by exteriorPower.map of that degree-one substitution, using the contraction formula to check the differential equation. The existing generator-chain-map declaration supplies the contraction formula and the construction pattern, but its stated component formula is only at the top degree; the all-degree formula required here is part of this new theorem. Modulo I these components are the exterior powers of the conormal coordinate change. Hom into B transposes them, so the comparison maps agree. Homotopy independence for projective resolution comparisons removes substitution choices; localization preserves all formulas. Refine arbitrary intersections by affine subopens to check that the local maps agree on all smaller opens using sheaf separatedness. The coordinate comparison is an isomorphism of the two finite free sheaves, and thus its component on every smaller open is surjective, including non-affine opens. Choose a neighborhood of each point inside its chart and restrict the comparison there. This gives the compatible family and its section surjectivity. Global morphism gluing is left to the parent. Compare derived universes using a common K-injective Hom model. Degree zero gives the quotient unit; degrees above chart length have zero target; empty V is vacuous. No global inverse or injectivity assertion is part of this step.

lean.statement:
theorem koszulRegularImmersion_self_ext_conormal_local_comparison
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (V : Z.Opens) (n : ℕ)
    (hregular : ∀ z : Z, z ∈ V → ∃ U : Y.affineOpens, i z ∈ U.1 ∧
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
        Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    let T := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G)
    let F := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      (Scheme.Modules.dual (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf
        ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules) n))
    ∃ (W : V.toScheme → V.toScheme.Opens)
      (φ : ∀ z : V.toScheme, F.over (W z) ⟶ T.over (W z)),
      (∀ z : V.toScheme, z ∈ W z) ∧
      (∀ (x y : V.toScheme) (U : V.toScheme.Opens)
        (hx : U ≤ W x) (hy : U ≤ W y),
        (φ x).val.app (op (Over.mk (homOfLE hx))) =
          (φ y).val.app (op (Over.mk (homOfLE hy)))) ∧
      (∀ (x : V.toScheme) (U : V.toScheme.Opens) (hx : U ≤ W x),
        Function.Surjective ((φ x).val.app (op (Over.mk (homOfLE hx)))))
